a combination of a charge-orbital ordered state and a tendency to magnetic dimerization leads to a large polarization.

The main takeaway from our work is that
ferroelectricity can be driven by purely magnetic degrees of freedom in a wide variety of multiferroics, which is of fundamental interest and may have important technological consequences.
ferroelectricity is not an exclusive property of insulators, and can be induced by magnetism in a wide variety of materials.
the presence of ferroelectricity is not limited to the canonical ferroelectric materials but can also be realized in materials that are not ferroelectric by symmetry.
